name: Ffynnon Beuno, Pen Dre (Holywell)
desc: A minor spring and pool in Holywell attributed to St Beuno, uncle of St Winefride; the Royal Commission noted only a slight spring here in 1912.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Wen, Trelawnyd
desc: Stone-built well chamber with a twin structure beside a pond inside a polygonal enclosure; much of the setting was dug out after 2001 to make a duck pond, exposing the footings. On private land.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Mihangel / St Michael's Well, Cilcain
desc: Holy well dedicated to St Michael, already ruinous when Edward Lhuyd noted it c.1700; now just a shallow overgrown hollow.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fair, Halkyn
desc: St Mary's well in the south corner of Halkyn old churchyard: a round stone basin recorded by Lhuyd in 1699, now capped with slabs that are probably reused gravestones.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Leinw, Cilcain
desc: Medieval stone-lined well basin long credited with medicinal water, traditionally linked to Gerald of Wales's journey through the area in 1188.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Mihangel, Caerwys
desc: Spring rising in a natural limestone basin near Caerwys, dedicated to St Michael and listed by Edward Lhuyd c.1699.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Deg, Caerwys
desc: Rectangular walled well enclosure about 8 by 4 yards outside Caerwys, recorded by Edward Lhuyd; on farmland.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fair / St Mary's Well, Cwm Vicarage
desc: Well dedicated to the Virgin by the old vicarage at Cwm, mentioned by Edward Lhuyd around 1700; little is recorded of its present state. Location approximate.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Ddier / Ffynnon Deifer, Bodfari
desc: Holy well of St Deifer (Dier), the original patron of Bodfari church; once a resort for sick children, it is now a neglected spring.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gynhafal / St Cynhafal's Well
desc: Wart-curing well of St Cynhafal near Llangynhafal, praised in a late-medieval poem; the present chamber is a modern rebuild tied to field drainage. On private land.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Oerog / Holy Well, Trevor
desc: The strongest of a cluster of cold springs near Trevor, Llangollen, enclosed in a small brick surround and once much visited by sufferers of rheumatism.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fair / St Melyd's Well, Meliden
desc: Small boundary well between Meliden and Gwaenysgor associated with St Mary and the local saint Melyd; now largely dry.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fael a Sulien, Cwm
desc: Medicinal spring by Cwm vicarage named for the paired saints Mael and Sulien; steps lead down to water protected by an old grave slab, renovated in 1772.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Garmon's Well, Llandegla
desc: Stone-lined spring under a bank on a disused road, walled on three sides, dedicated to St Garmon (Germanus); a cross wall once ponded the outflow.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Benno, Gwyddelwern
desc: Sunken slate-lined well enclosure regarded as a sacred well of St Beuno, about 6 by 5 feet and 3 feet deep.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Asa, Cwm (Dyserth)
desc: Powerful spring of St Asaph, said in Lhuyd's day to ebb and flow and to rival Holywell in volume, once framed by pillars and driving a mill; now absorbed into a modern reservoir.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Mordeyrn's Well, Nantglyn
desc: Site of the well of St Mordeyrn, patron of Nantglyn church, about 250 yards north of the church; the ground is still damp but no structure survives.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Trillo, Llandrillo (Edeirnion)
desc: Spring roughly 420m north of St Trillo's church in Llandrillo, Edeirnion, named for the church's saint and shown on 1890s OS maps. Distinct from St Trillo's Chapel at Rhos-on-Sea.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Dogfan's Holy Well (upland site)
desc: Peat-cut, stone-ended trough fed by clear seepage on open moorland, identified as a site of St Dogfan's well; recorded from air photographs in 2007.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Mary's Well, Betws Gwerfil Goch
desc: Well dedicated to the Virgin that Lhuyd placed 'a stone's throw from the church' of Betws Gwerfil Goch.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Mary's Well and Bath, Bodrhyddan
desc: Ornate octagonal well house with cupola and pelican finial plus a balustraded bath in the grounds of Bodrhyddan Hall; it bears a spurious 'Inigo Jones 1612' inscription but seems to be 18th century. Private estate.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Beuno, Tremeirchion
desc: Medieval bathing well of St Beuno below the Ffynnon Beuno caves: a walled pool whose overflow spouts through a worn carved stone head. Beside a private house.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Sara, Derwen
desc: Open spring with three stone steps down to the water near Derwen, recorded by Lhuyd in 1698; traditionally a healing well for rheumatism.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Tysilio, Bryneglwys
desc: Well of St Tysilio noted by Edward Lhuyd in 1698 near Bryneglwys; its precise position is now uncertain (location approximate).
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Wen, Trefnant
desc: Ruined spring complex near Trefnant with a well, bath house and a dressing room with fireplace, showing its use as a bathing well.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Sadwrn, Denbigh
desc: Well of St Sadwrn near Denbigh, recorded by Lhuyd in 1698; a low footstone fronts a chamber protected by rough walling.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Farchweil, Denbigh
desc: Old well near Denbigh noted by Edward Lhuyd in 1698; only the channel that carried its outflow survives.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Elidan, Llanelidan
desc: Well of St Elidan near Cefn-y-wern farm, Llanelidan; it has silted up and its exact site is lost (location approximate).
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fair, Penycae
desc: Spring dedicated to St Mary rising in a field named after it on the Plas Du land, documented in a 1620 survey; no surviving traditions.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon y Saint / Saints' Well, Bangor-on-Dee
desc: Spring near Hopyard Coppice, probably the 'Ffynnon y Saint' Lhuyd recorded in 1698 in Bangor Monachorum parish, home of the famous early monastery.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Holy Well, Burton (Rossett)
desc: Once a famous spring and a fixed point on the medieval England-Wales boundary, recorded in 1448; now only faint boggy traces.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Peter's Well, Rossett
desc: Well of the former St Peter's chapel, some 450 yards from the chapel site; choked but the spring still runs.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gynfran, Llysfaen
desc: Holy well of St Cynfran, said to have been visited to cure sick cattle; now a sludge-filled basin half ringed by a drystone wall in a hedge bank.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Tudno's Well, Great Orme
desc: Well named for St Tudno, the 6th-century hermit whose church stands on the Great Orme above Llandudno.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Cegidog / St George's Well
desc: Railed holy well at St George near Abergele, made up of a spring pool and a masonry tank; horses were traditionally brought here to be blessed.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Santes Fair, Llanrhos
desc: Small half-round stone basin capped with a slab behind a housing estate about 150m from Llanrhos church; rediscovered only in 1993.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Asa, Llannefydd
desc: Spring feeding the River Asa, recorded by Lhuyd c.1698 and probably dedicated to St Asaph; no structure survives.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Asa, Eglwysbach
desc: St Asaph's well in Eglwysbach, documented from 1648, closed in the 19th century and replaced by a village pump; its overflow still wets the meadow.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Ddoged, Llanddoged
desc: Well of St Doged, an enclosed basin covered by two large slabs, listed by Lhuyd in 1698.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Digain, Llangernyw
desc: Parish well of St Digain at Llangernyw (home of the ancient yew), a slab-lined chamber covered in masonry.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gelynin, Llangelynnin
desc: Holy well beside the remote old church of Llangelynnin above the Conwy valley: a walled basin in a ruined well house said to be dated 1622; reputed to cure sick children.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Armon, Llanarmon (Bro Garmon)
desc: Overgrown well of St Garmon in rough masonry about 500m north-east of the church.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Nefydd, Llannefydd
desc: Spring of St Nefydd roughly 300 yards from Llannefydd church.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Wnnod, Llangwm
desc: Spring in a bank once protected by two flagstones, recorded by Lhuyd in 1698; now in a modern brick chamber.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Eidda, Bro Machno
desc: Roadside upland well at 484m by the B4407, in a stone-roofed shelter inscribed 'Yf a bydd ddiolchgar' (drink and be thankful), rebuilt 1846.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Arian, Llanengan
desc: Natural spring with no structure, recorded by Francis Jones as a wishing well.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gwynedd, Llannor
desc: Holy well once enclosed in big drystone walls about 8 feet square; now concreted over.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Frothen, Llanfrothen
desc: Possible site of the well of St Brothen by the stream near Llanfrothen church, noted by Lhuyd c.1698 and later described as walled on three sides.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Ddwrdan, Aberdaron
desc: Holy well on the Llŷn pilgrim route to Bardsey, now a pool of probable artificial origin with no visible masonry.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fair, Buan
desc: St Mary's well near Boduan, originally three-cornered but now heavily modernised as a tank.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gower, Llangower
desc: Spring of St Gywer in boggy ground about 650m from Llangower church by Llyn Tegid, once paired with a standing stone, Llech Gower; hard to locate.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Ddunawd, Dolbenmaen
desc: Stone-lined well chamber cut into a bank at the corner of a ruined building, below Braich y Saint.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Grasi, Llyn Glasfryn
desc: Walled, dilapidated well at the north-east corner of Llyn Glasfryn; legend says a maid named Grassi left it uncovered and its overflow created the lake.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Y Ffynnon, Ffestiniog
desc: Spring under a ruined house that issues through an iron pipe; no saint is linked to it but its water was thought to be remedial.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Saint, Bron Llwyd (Aberdaron)
desc: Square stone-walled pool on Bron Llwyd hill, probably with steps, used by pilgrims bound for Bardsey.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Derfel, Llandderfel
desc: Spring of St Derfel about 350m from Llandderfel church, once protected by slate and rough masonry forming a small reservoir.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Lleuddad, Botwnnog
desc: Spring dedicated to St Lleuddad of Bardsey, partly banked and formerly walled; masonry shows when it is cleared.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gadfan / St Cadfan's Wells, Tywyn
desc: Well of St Cadfan near his church in Tywyn, noted in 1535; converted into two baths with dressing rooms before the 1850s and reputed to cure skin ailments and rheumatism.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Deiniol, Llanfor
desc: Small walled well of St Deiniol just north-east of Llanfor churchyard, whose water flowed through the churchyard.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Elen, Llanfrothen
desc: Roadside well on the Roman road Sarn Helen, named after Elen of the legend; no medieval tradition recorded.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Garmon, Betws Garmon
desc: Spring by the presumed chapel of St Garmon, now buried in dense forestry, with scattered stones from a former cover.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fair, Llanfair (Harlech)
desc: Sunken well with stone steps, sharing its dedication with St Mary's church 260m away; an older ruined well is also reported nearby.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Bedrog, Llanbedrog
desc: Small rubble-lined well of St Pedrog, known locally as 'The Wishing Well'.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Aelhaearn, Llanaelhaearn
desc: Holy well of St Aelhaearn by the church, a medieval basin with stone benches covered by a well house inscribed 'Roofed 1900'; later used for water supply.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Cawdraf, Llannor
desc: Well dedicated to St Cawdraf, now covered by a small modern brick structure on what may be old slabs.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Engan, Llanengan
desc: Probable holy well of St Einion (Engan), a water-filled walled basin about 3m square.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Cwm Rhwyfor, Tal-y-llyn
desc: Medicinal well in the Tal-y-llyn valley below Cadair Idris.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Dudwen, Llaniestyn
desc: Spring basin backed by a curved drystone revetment, linked with St Tudwen's church at Llandudwen.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Saint, Aberdaron (Bardsey route)
desc: Small D-shaped walled well near Aberdaron with a hinged iron lid, still in use in the 1960s but now overgrown.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Garmon, Y Felinheli
desc: Well of St Garmon said to cure rheumatism and skin complaints; later used to supply cottages below.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Pistyll Holy Well
desc: Well near the pilgrim church of St Beuno at Pistyll, known locally as the 'Holy Well'; no ancient features visible.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon y Capel, Llanfachreth
desc: Large square walled well enclosure with five steps down, valued for medicinal properties.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Rhedyw, Llanllyfni
desc: Rectangular basin with steps enclosing a natural spring, dedicated to St Rhedyw of Llanllyfni.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Decwyn, Talsarnau
desc: Spring flowing into a rock cistern, probably the well of St Tecwyn listed by Lhuyd.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gadfarch, Llannor
desc: Holy well of St Cadfarch near Llannor, modernised with its water diverted into pipes.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Mary's Well, Nefyn
desc: Ornate square stone well house built by the Nefyn Corporation in 1868, with slate inscriptions and a pyramid roof, in Stryd y Ffynnon on the Bardsey pilgrim route.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Oledd, Llanelltyd
desc: Round walled well with steps down, traditionally held to have curative powers.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Betws Fawr Well, Llanystumdwy
desc: Keyhole-shaped holy well: a covered round chamber that feeds a long boulder-lined pool cut into the slope.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Saint (St Catherine's), Criccieth
desc: Former well dedicated to St Catherine, noted for curing eye infections; filled in around 1962 when a garage was built.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fyw, Mynytho
desc: Walled bathing well with stone seats, main bath and drinking tank, restored c.1890; linked to St Curig and said to cure blindness.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fair, Bryncroes
desc: Ancient rectangular well with probably 17th-century steps on three sides near St Mary's church, Bryncroes.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Beris, Nant Peris
desc: Holy well of St Peris by the old church in Nant Peris, with slate steps around a basin and wall niches; its sacred fish were said to foretell cures.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Aelrhiw, Rhiw
desc: Stone-walled square enclosure with steps and seats around a sunken basin near Rhiw, probably 17th century.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Faglan, Llanfaglan
desc: Well of St Baglan near Llanfaglan, once a stone basin with a wide seat around it; now two low walls and a hollow.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Mihangel, Llanfihangel-y-pennant
desc: Old well of St Michael on the slope of Mynydd Tyn-y-fach: a boulder-walled trench, its flow partly diverted by a modern cutting.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Badrig, Dyffryn Ardudwy
desc: Spring named for St Patrick with no masonry; legend ties the saint to the nearby coast.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Enddwyn, Llanenddwyn
desc: Well and bath of St Enddwyn in rough masonry, probably once roofed, said to have healed the saint herself; now choked.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Cwmtwrch (Ffynnon Ddrewllyd), Corris
desc: Pungent sulphur spring beside cottages on the Afon Twrch, a popular local spa in the early 1900s with eisteddfodau held alongside; restored 1920 and 1993.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Bryn Fendigaid, Aberffraw
desc: Medicinal well near Aberffraw; no trace now survives.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Badrig, Llanbadrig
desc: Well of St Patrick near Llanbadrig church, where the saint is said to have come ashore; noted for cures, its remains were destroyed by a storm in 1967.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gredifael, Penmynydd
desc: Site of St Credifael's well, once a spring-fed masonry basin by a pond; levelled by 1986.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gaffo, Llangaffo
desc: Holy well of St Caffo near Llangaffo, destroyed when the railway was built.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Eilian, Llaneilian (Anglesey)
desc: Cliff-foot spring of St Eilian near Point Lynas, visited on the saint's day, with traces of a possible well chapel. Not the Llanelian-yn-Rhos cursing well.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Seiriol, Pont Clorach
desc: Healing well of St Seiriol at Pont Clorach where Seiriol and Cybi were said to meet; filled in when the bridge was built in 1840.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Nidan, Llanidan
desc: Stone-lined spring in the grounds of Llanidan Hall, traditionally St Nidan's well, linked to his church; private estate.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Cybi's Well, Holyhead
desc: Healing well associated with St Cybi near his church in the Roman fort at Holyhead; legend says it sprang where the saint struck the ground.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Crochan Llanddwyn wishing well
desc: Small reputed wishing well connected with Llanddwyn and St Dwynwen; destroyed by reservoir construction.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Beuno, Aberffraw
desc: Site of St Beuno's well at Aberffraw, latterly under a brick pump house; now beneath the road.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Ddygfael, Mechell
desc: Boarded-over well shaft about 160m from the site of Llanddygfael church.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Ddaniel, Llanddaniel Fab
desc: Well dedicated to St Deiniol Fab credited with healing waters. Location approximate.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gybi, Pont Clorach
desc: Healing well of St Cybi opposite Ffynnon Seiriol at Pont Clorach, where the two saints were said to meet each week; its water now mingles with the stream.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Allgo, Llanallgo
desc: Pretty well of St Allgo by a stream 350m from Llanallgo church: a small stone enclosure with benches round a pool.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gybi, Llannerch-y-medd
desc: Alleged holy well of St Cybi, a low angle of walling cutting off a field corner; no known traditions.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Ceinwen, Cerrigceinwen
desc: Natural rock well on the south side of Cerrigceinwen churchyard, dedicated to St Ceinwen and credited with healing.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Myllin, Llanfyllin
desc: Holy well of St Myllin above Llanfyllin, where the saint is said to have baptised by immersion; later a closed parish well.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Trinity Well, Arddleen
desc: Traditional meeting place on Trinity Sunday at Arddleen; no longer a public well.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Eluned's Chapel and Well, Slwch
desc: Scheduled site of St Eluned's oratory and holy well near Slwch Tump outside Brecon, scene of a lively medieval saint's-day festival; now platforms by a damp hollow.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fair, Llanfair Caereinion
desc: St Mary's well at the foot of steps from the churchyard to the River Banwy, long thought curative; restored in 1990 within a small garden.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Erfyl, Llanerfyl
desc: Spring on the bank of the Banwy at Llanerfyl whose water was used for baptisms at St Erfyl's church.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Tydecho's Well, Banwy
desc: Well of St Tydecho, now filled; it once had a carved stone saint's head that has been lost.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Dogfan, Llanwddyn
desc: Well of St Dogfan once used to cure eye disease; now flows into Lake Vyrnwy.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Dol-y-Coed Sulphur Well, Llanwrtyd Wells
desc: Sulphur spring found in 1732 by Rev. Theophilus Evans that launched Llanwrtyd as a spa; a later well house stands in the Dol-y-Coed Hotel grounds.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Michael's Well, Llanfihangel-yng-Ngwynfa
desc: Disused well whose water was formerly used for baptisms at St Michael's church.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Dinas Well, Castell Dinas
desc: Embanked muddy pond inside the Castell Dinas hillfort, traditionally curative for skin diseases.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Isel, Llanwddyn
desc: Copious spring reputed to heal infant ailments, now feeding Lake Vyrnwy.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gattwg, Llangattock
desc: Spring of St Cadog issuing from an iron pipe in a field wall, with the associations of a medieval holy well.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ladywell, Berriew
desc: Well dedicated to Our Lady, once provided with a can on a chain; filled in though the spring still runs.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: The Saint's Well, Abbey Cwmhir
desc: Open spring rising into a natural stone basin at the foot of a 30-foot rock face near Abbey Cwmhir.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Ddewi, Abergwesyn
desc: Holy well of St David near Llanddewi Abergwesyn church, recorded in Lhuyd's Parochialia.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Armon, Llanfechain
desc: Ancient holy well of St Garmon, built round with stone and slab-covered, once used for baptism and bathing.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Tysilio's Spout, Welshpool
desc: The 'Fons Tessilian' of a 1202 charter, linked to St Tysilio; concreted over with an inspection cover by 1981.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Blaen-Edw Sulphur Well, Glascwm
desc: Medicinal sulphur well above the River Edw in a ruined, probably Victorian stone well chamber.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnonau Penegoes (St Cadfarch's)
desc: Two medicinal wells of St Cadfarch facing each other across the road at Penegoes, each in low stone walls.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Black Well, Aberhafesp
desc: Chalybeate (iron-rich) spring visited for healing, though without any saintly dedication.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Ishow, Partrishow
desc: Well of St Issui below the remote church of Partrishow: a drystone, slab-roofed chamber with small niches, where offerings are still left.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Trinity Well, Guilsfield
desc: Spring at the foot of a rock on Gaer Fawr, frequented on Trinity Sunday.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gynidr, Glasbury
desc: Holy well of St Cynidr with an open well house of c.1900-1910.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon y Ffinnant, Llanfechain
desc: Flagged well with steps and a small modern hut, said to have curative powers.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Monk's Well, Clyro
desc: Holy well said to cure eye complaints, adapted for domestic supply under a concrete slab.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Cwm Ewyn, Llangynog
desc: Stone-lined healing well with steps, possibly rebuilt about 1900.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Geiliog (Cock Well), Llanfihangel
desc: Trinity Sunday gathering place near Llys-y-Cawr, with cock fighting held nearby.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Wtra Heilyn, Llanfihangel
desc: Walled basin on a stream bank, once roofed and used for bathing.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Jacket's Well / St Edward's Well, Knighton
desc: Healing well for sprains and rheumatism; the name is thought to come from Welsh 'iachâd' (healing).
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fadog, Llanfair Caereinion
desc: Mineral spring of later repute with an older holy well close by.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Drewi, Elan Valley
desc: Possible holy well shown on the 1891 map, now under the Elan reservoir and perhaps visible at low water.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Holy Well, Pilleth
desc: Holy well on the north side of St Mary's church at Pilleth, credited with curing eye ailments.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fair, Beguildy
desc: St Mary's well in a modern fenced enclosure with a hawthorn beside it; no pre-20th-century fabric visible.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fair, Partrishow
desc: Holy well called Ffynnon Fair recorded by Francis Jones in Partrishow parish; its identification is uncertain.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Cadfan's Well, Llangadfan
desc: Curative well of St Cadfan in a recess under the road near the church; its well house was lost to road building.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Beuno's Well (St Bennion's), Carreghofa
desc: Holy well described as neglected in 1910; now a modern spring chamber.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Dogfan's Well, Llanrhaeadr-ym-Mochnant
desc: Spring about 150 yards from St Dogfan's church, reputed for healing.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Pistyll Gwyn, Machynlleth
desc: Medicinal well on Pen yr Allt common believed to cure sprains.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: David's Well, Llanbadarn Fynydd
desc: Partly stone-lined spring much frequented for medicinal water, known as the well of David the smith.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Illog, Hirnant
desc: Natural spring once renowned for curative properties, later piped to the rectory.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Silin, Llansilin
desc: Former roadside spring of St Silin near Ty'n-llan, now dry; the old chamber was filled in.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fair, Rhayader
desc: Spout well of local repute dedicated to the Virgin; its stone bowl was removed when the Aberystwyth road was built.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon y Myneich, Llanwddyn
desc: Plentiful spring south of the ruined monastic hospice at Llanwddyn (the monks' well).
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Ddewi, Llandysiliogogo
desc: Traditional holy well of St David.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Glasffrwd Holy Well, Ystrad Fflur
desc: Slate-lined trench and cistern in forestry near Strata Florida, regarded as a holy well.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Gwenhafdre Uchaf Holy Well, Ystrad Meurig
desc: Unusual pyramid-shaped stone well house with a horseshoe chamber, said to have been used by monks walking to and from Strata Florida.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Holy Well, St Michael's, Llandre
desc: Holy well beside Llanfihangel Genau'r Glyn churchyard, visited by the sick; a crippled girl was said to have walked away cured shortly before 1911. Basin uncovered in 1975.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Badarn, Aberystwyth
desc: Chalybeate spring found in 1779 on the Llanbadarn road and later housed as a drinking fountain.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gybi / Ffynnon Wen, Llangybi (Ceredigion)
desc: Healing well of St Cybi; the sick bathed here then slept on the Llech Gybi capstone, and recovery or death was read from the result.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Bedr / Peterwell, Lampeter
desc: Once-famous well of St Peter at Lampeter that gave its name to the Peterwell mansion; now a stony hollow.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Drewi, Lledrod
desc: Three wells in a row 1.5m apart, each believed to have different properties.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Teilo's Well, Llandeilo Llwydiarth
desc: Healing well near ruined St Teilo's church whose water was drunk from the saint's skull, kept by the Melchior family until the 1920s.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Pistyll Dewi, Porthclais
desc: Holy spring once running beneath Capel y Pistyll, a pilgrimage chapel by the harbour where St David is said to have been baptised.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Govan's Well, Bosherston
desc: Stone-lined well below St Govan's cliff chapel, famous for curing lameness and eye disease; red clay nearby was used as a poultice. Now dry.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Mary's Well, Angle
desc: Covered clifftop well with a pump near the site of St Mary's chapel above Chapel Bay.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fyrnach, Llanfyrnach
desc: Spring of St Brynach reputed to heal.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Pistyll Dewi, St Davids Cathedral
desc: Site of St David's well by the cathedral close, said to have sprung after the saint prayed during a drought; no trace survives.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Llanllawer Holy Well, Llanychaer
desc: Spring in a deep rough-masonry chamber with reputed healing powers.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Mary's Well, St Davids Cathedral
desc: Site of St Mary's well beside Pistyll Dewi outside the cathedral close at St Davids.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Teilo's Well, Llangwathen
desc: Pond by a castle mound thought to mark the medieval well of St Teilo, linked to Llangwathen chapel.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gain, New Moat
desc: Holy well of St Ceinwen with slight traces of foundations.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Meugan's Well, Llanfair Nant-gwyn
desc: Strong spring where a well chapel of St Meugan once stood.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Margaret's Well, Templeton
desc: Stone well chamber with a corbelled roof set into a bank; listed by Francis Jones, last reported dry in 1975.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Caradog's Well, Haverfordwest
desc: Well of the hermit St Caradog, documented in 1315; concreted over in 1838 under a manhole.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gapan, Llanllawer
desc: Corbelled well chamber by Llanllawer church famed for curing sore eyes; pins and coins were left as offerings and bent pins thrown in as curses.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Mary's Churchyard Well, Burton
desc: Restored walled well in Burton churchyard near a medieval cross base, once used as a baptistery.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Leonard's Well, Rudbaxton Rath
desc: Dry well chamber in the rampart of Rudbaxton Rath beside the vanished chapel of St Leonard (recorded 1398).
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Degan's Well, Pencaer
desc: Stone-lined spring flowing to the sea near the site of Capel Degan.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Brynach's Well, Henry's Moat
desc: Water-filled hollow under a masonry hood next to the site of St Brynach's chapel, possibly early medieval.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Deilo, Crinow
desc: Spring flowing into a rough basin, said to heal.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Gumfreston Wells
desc: Three stone-edged springs in Gumfreston churchyard, two chalybeate and one pure, once visited for their healing water.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Justinian's Well, St Davids
desc: Stone well house about 40m from St Justinian's chapel facing Ramsey Island, now supplying a cottage.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Faiddog, St Davids
desc: Spring probably dedicated to St Aidan (Maedog); largely drained by road widening.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Wnda, Llanwnda
desc: Recently restored, signposted holy well of St Gwyndaf in woodland near Llanwnda church.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Olden, Little Newcastle
desc: Spring reputed for curative powers, though not a traditional sacred well.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Decuman's Well, Rhoscrowther
desc: Remains of a small walled chamber near St Decuman's church.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Dogfael's Well, Meline
desc: Spring 10m west of St Dogfael's church at Felindre Farchog.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Owen's Well, Narberth
desc: Limestone remains of a beehive-shaped well head, the Owen's Well recorded in 1698 near a lost early medieval inscribed stone.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Brynach's Well, Cilgwyn
desc: Possibly medieval well of St Brynach near early medieval cross-carved pillar stones.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Ddewi, Solva
desc: Curative spring on the St Davids pilgrim route, a small stone-lined cavity disused by 1964.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Nicholas's Well, Monkton
desc: Corbelled medieval well chamber reputedly supplying Pembroke Castle; possibly a conduit house for St Nicholas's Priory.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Higgon's Well, Haverfordwest
desc: Site of a renowned medieval holy well and well chapel with a vaulted chamber.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Ddewi, Llanddewi Velfrey
desc: Former spring of St David, now dry, near Llangwathen chapel.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon y Cwcwll, St Davids
desc: Corbelled beehive well about 8-9 feet deep close to St Davids Cathedral; door blocked in 1950.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fair, Capel Mair (Llangeler)
desc: St Mary's well in Cae Ffynnon Fair about 420m from Capel Mair.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Geler, Llangeler
desc: Spring of St Celert that once had a well chapel below the church, at the foot of Allt Geler.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Frynach, Llanboidy
desc: Small well chamber of St Brynach, said only to be 'good for sick people'.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Saint, Llansaint
desc: Holy well about 300m from All Saints church, later topped by the village pump.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Capel Bigawdin well chapel, Porthyrhyd
desc: Ruined, possibly 14th-century well chapel at the edge of woodland near Bigawdin farm.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Sul, Kidwelly
desc: Spring behind Kidwelly Castle, said to have risen where a prince was slain; recorded from 1587.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gwenno, Pumsaint
desc: Healing well near the Dolaucothi gold mines, haunted by Gwenno, who was said to have been imprisoned under the crag by spirits.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Llawddog's Well, Cenarth
desc: Well of St Llawddog by the Teifi near Cenarth church, under a modern brick cover.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Anthony's Well, Llansteffan
desc: Well head with a simple stone arch and an empty niche that once held a saint's image; a pin-wishing well.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon y Capel, Llangathen
desc: Small woodland well near the lost Capel Pen Arw, once highly regarded for cures.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Canna's Well, Whitland
desc: Healing spring linked with St Canna's church and the nearby St Canna's Chair stone.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Mihangel, Kidwelly
desc: Well of St Michael beside the site of Capel Mihangel, documented from 1575.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Stockwell, Llanboidy
desc: Hillside well where water was drunk with sugar and pins dropped in for good wishes.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Tybie's Well, Llandybie
desc: Spring of St Tybie about half a mile from Llandybie church.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Five Saints Wells, Llanpumsaint
desc: Five rock pools in Cwm Cerwyni, said to match the five saints of Llanpumsaint church.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Capel Herbach well chapel, Gorslas
desc: Ruined, possibly 14th-century well chapel beside a stream at Banc-y-Mansel.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Dyfan's Well, Llandyfan
desc: Churchyard well-baptistery of St Dyfan, visited by pilgrims who stayed at the inn next door.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Iago, Llanybydder
desc: St James's well close to the site of the vanished Capel Iago.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon y Mêr, Kenfig Burrows
desc: Spring on Kenfig Burrows in a D-shaped limestone surround, said to be St David's; restored 1985.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St David's Well, Nottage
desc: D-shaped stone well enclosure partly roofed with slabs, repaired about 1932.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Lygad, Kenfig
desc: Natural spring venerated as a holy well for curing eye disease.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St John's Well (Sandford's Well), Newton
desc: Tidal underground well near Newton church whose level falls as the tide rises; a miracle-working well and 1920s open-air spa.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fawr, Nottage
desc: Probably a restored medieval well in a walled enclosure near the site of Nottage chapel.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Sant Sannan, Argoed
desc: Rubble-stone well chamber of St Sannan with a modern superstructure.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gattwg, Pentyrch
desc: Spring of St Cadog issuing from a pipe in a retaining wall.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Fagans Well
desc: Stone-enclosed spring near St Fagans, probably the healing well noted gushing from the rock in 1645.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Teilo's / Dairy Well, Llandaff
desc: Covered well in the Cathedral School grounds associated with St Euddogwy, Teilo's nephew.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Brecon Road Well, Merthyr Tydfil
desc: Probable holy well found in a house cellar on Brecon Road; now filled in.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Dudful / Tydfil's Well, Merthyr
desc: Lost well in Well Street named after the martyr Tudful, daughter of Brychan.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gybi, Llangybi (Monmouthshire)
desc: Medieval vaulted well chamber of St Cybi outside Llangybi churchyard, with interior niches; still intact.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Bride's Well, Skenfrith
desc: Copious spring of St Ffraid that once filled a walled pool.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Angoeron, Goetre
desc: Small stone chamber with slab cap, credited with healing; bent pins, coins and buttons were found here in the 1890s.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Tewdric's Well, Mathern
desc: Fenced well with steps down where King Tewdrig's wounds were said to have been washed before his death.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Virtuous Well (St Anne's), Trellech
desc: Horseshoe-shaped walled well with a bench and corbelled niche, popular in the 17th century; rags are still tied to the nearby tree. Guardianship site.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Lady's Well, Margam
desc: Spring in a drystone setting near Margam Abbey.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Iago, Margam
desc: Possible holy well of St James near the farm of the same name (location approximate).
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Gyffyr, Margam
desc: Vaulted bath house on the Cwm Bach, possibly first a baptistery for Hen Eglwys and later a cold bath for Margam Abbey.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Arian, Baglan
desc: Spring with trough, probably the well where sickly children were taken in the 19th century.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Margaret's Well, Coedffranc
desc: Lost well at the foot of the rise where St Margaret's chapel stood.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Bedr, Margam
desc: Spring flowing through a stone culvert, perhaps supplying Margam Abbey.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Wilcrick Well, Magor
desc: Small vaulted wishing well by the path to Wilcrick church.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Rhingyll, Eglwysilan
desc: Holy well of the Eglwysilan parish (location approximate, given at the farm of the same name).
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Fair, Penrhys
desc: Stone well house over the spring at Penrhys, a major late medieval pilgrimage centre to the Virgin; restored and still visited.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Tarren Deusant, Llantrisant
desc: Spring beside rock-carved figures of 'two saints' recorded in 1696, regarded as a possible holy well or pagan shrine.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Peter's Well, Caswell
desc: Walled spring excavated in 1895 with the remains of the medieval chapel and priest's house in Bishopston valley.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Holy Well, Cefn Bryn
desc: Bubbling spring on Cefn Bryn, perhaps the curative well where pins were left as offerings.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Trinity Well / St Cenydd's Well, Ilston
desc: Well inside the ruined Trinity Well Chapel (c.1649-60, Wales's oldest Baptist chapel) on the site of St Cenydd's medieval chapel.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Deilo, Pendoylan
desc: Walled spring basin of St Teilo used as a garden feature in 1956.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon Dyfrig, Llancarfan
desc: Spring of St Dyfrig with traces of a rubble structure in a hillside recess.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Anne's Well, Llanmihangel
desc: Rectangular stone chamber with a carved panel, linked to the Llanmihangel Place gardens.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St Mary's Well, Llanfair (Vale)
desc: Holy well north of St Mary's church at Llanfair, a slab-covered chamber with an attached brick cistern.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: St John's Well, St Athan
desc: Holy well at Beggars Bound, walled and railed.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Holy Well, Coedrhydyglyn
desc: Roadside well on the way to Peterston reputed to cure eye disorders (location approximate).
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon y Green, St Athan
desc: Holy well said to cure sore eyes if bathed in before sunrise (location approximate).
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Llancarfan Holy Well
desc: Holy well said to cure scrofula (the King's Evil).
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)

name: Ffynnon y Drindod, Llandow
desc: Trinity spring near the source of the Afon Alun with possible traces of stonework.
source: Coflein (RCAHMW National Monuments Record of Wales)
